description: Defense-in-depth command policy. Unreal generation, cooking, packaging, and similar high-privilege commands are never treated as generally safe. They require explicit per-handoff permission, assigned generated output ownership, and will be audited. Discovered commands only; no invention of paths or wrappers. AUTHORITATIVE DECLARATION (R-PROT-1, 2026-07-29): the 'classifier' block below is the single source of truth for the protected set and the lexer's tables; CommandPolicy.psm1 reads them from here and hardcodes none of them, and Assert-BashPolicy.ps1 reads 'blocked_patterns' and 'vendor_content_patterns' from here rather than duplicating them.

blocked_patterns.reason: No remote mutations or PRs from any agent. Orchestrator coordinates branches locally only.

History rewrite forbidden. (2026-07-29: the previous alternative was 'git\s+amend', which matched a command git does not have and never matched the real 'git commit --amend'. Aligned with Assert-ActionPolicy.ps1's irreversible-pattern list; the --am(e(n(d)?)?) tail also covers git's unambiguous option abbreviations --am/--ame/--amen.)
Pipe-to-shell or remote code execution vector.

vendor_content_patterns.reason: Command appears to target vendor/sample content (read-only per content_policy.json).

classifier.comment: Tables consumed by CommandPolicy.psm1. Adding a protected target here MUST NOT require editing the lexer (R-PROT-4). Names are compared lower-case after Win32 canonicalisation (trailing dots and whitespace trimmed) and, for 'protected_basenames'/'protected_basename_patterns', after stripping one executable suffix matched by 'executable_suffix_pattern'. 'protected_filenames' are compared WITH their suffix, for targets whose bare stem is too generic to protect safely (build, cook).

protected_subcommands.reason: LFS operations on binaries should be controlled; avoid in workers (R-PROT-3). Matched only when 'git' holds a proven command position and 'lfs' is its first subcommand, so 'git commit -m "ran git lfs pull"' stays data. git's own global options are skipped first (with their values, per global_value_flags) so 'git -C submodule lfs pull' still matches.

stdin_executors.comment: R-STDIN-1: a heredoc / here-string body redirected into one of these is scanned as COMMANDS, not data. Membership alone is not enough - the module also inspects the owning command's own arguments, because 'bash -c x <<EOF' and 'bash script.sh <<EOF' both make stdin data again.

read_only: Basic repository reads, git status/log/diff (within worktree), text inspection of .uproject/Config/Content (text parts only).
text_verification: Schema validation, JSON/YAML linting, custom project-owned text validators (when they exist under factory roots).
unreal_command_classification.compile: Project build+test oracle is gate.ps1 (repo root): builds GloamsteadEditor Win64 Development via UE 5.8 Build.bat then runs 'Automation RunTests Gloamstead' and fails closed on the report. Writes only to Intermediate/Binaries and the TEMP report dir; no content mutation. Whitelisted (see whitelisted_commands). Requires the editor closed (LNK1104 otherwise).
unreal_command_classification.editor_generation: Whitelisted: agent_collab/scripts/Invoke-GloamsteadDataAssetImport.ps1 with -Manifest under specs/data/. Underlying UnrealEditor-Cmd -run=GloamsteadImportDataAssets only via that wrapper.
unreal_command_classification.map_load: No discovered command-line map validator. Requires human Editor/PIE load with evidence capture.
unreal_command_classification.automation_test: Automation tests run via gate.ps1 (UnrealEditor-Cmd -ExecCmds 'Automation RunTests Gloamstead'), report parsed and failed-closed. 16 Gloamstead C++ tests as of 2026-07-10; note all PCG tests use the synthetic Test_SeedPointStates seam, none exercise live InitializeFromPCGComponent.
unreal_command_classification.functional_test: No discovered functional test infrastructure. Requires human.
unreal_command_classification.package_smoke: No discovered cook or package scripts. Requires human.
unreal_command_classification.integration_verification: Combination of applicable profiles above + Critic audit of diff and binary file list. UE-dependent steps currently require human.
requires_human_approval: Any command that would install plugins, change EngineAssociation, download/purchase assets, accept licenses.

UnrealEditor-Cmd, RunUAT, BuildCookRun, or any cooking/packaging/automation command (even if the binary exists on the local machine) until explicitly whitelisted for a specific task with assigned generated_output_ownership.
forbidden: Commands that write to Intermediate/, Saved/, DerivedDataCache/, Binaries/ from within scripts.
Direct modification of .uasset/.umap etc. outside of approved automation on an owned task branch.

enforcement_notes: Shell policy is defense-in-depth only. Authoritative controls are: runtime capability validation in registry, exclusive Orchestrator lease, explicit handoff file_ownership + generated_output_ownership, edit-scope guards, worktree isolation, vendor immutability, structured result validation, Critic binary audits, and candidate integration verification.

whitelisted_commands.reason: Approved Data Asset factory wrapper (VS-POLISH-FACTORY-DATA-01). Must use -Manifest under specs/data/. NOTE (2026-07-29): this is DOCUMENTATION, not an enforcement short-circuit. Assert-BashPolicy.ps1 used to 'exit 0' on a substring match of this pattern anywhere in the command, which made any string containing it a universal off switch ('echo x # Invoke-GloamsteadDataAssetImport.ps1' passed every rule). That short-circuit is removed: the wrapper is a .ps1 script path, so the classifier allows it natively under R-NEST-2 with no bypass required.

Approved build+test oracle (2026-07-10 rebaseline). Builds GloamsteadEditor + runs Gloamstead automation tests, fails closed on the report. Reversible: writes only Intermediate/Binaries + TEMP report, no content or history mutation. Requires the editor closed. Also documentation only: 'pwsh -File gate.ps1' is allowed by R-NEST-2, not by a whitelist bypass.
